record.original_question: Study the transformations that preserve random strings and random sequences.

evidence.quote: 11. Study the transformations that preserve random strings and sequences. (C. Calude, H. Jürgensen)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma = \{0,1\}$. For a finite string $x \in \Sigma^*$, let $K(x)$ denote its (prefix-free) Kolmogorov complexity. A finite string $x$ of length $n$ is called (Kolmogorov/Chaitin) random if $K(x) \ge n - O(1)$ (with a suitable fixed constant). An infinite sequence $\omega \in \Sigma^\omega$ is called Martin-Löf random if it passes every Martin-Löf test, equivalently if there exists $c$ such that $K(\omega \upharpoonright n) \ge n - c$ for all $n$.

Characterize the class of transformations that preserve randomness in the following two senses:

1. (Finite case) Describe all maps $f : \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ (for example, computable maps, or maps induced by morphisms, codings, or finite transducers) such that there exists a constant $c$ for which: whenever $x$ is random with parameter $c_0$ (i.e.\ $K(x) \ge |x| - c_0$), the image $f(x)$ is random with parameter depending only on $c_0$ and $f$.

2. (Infinite case) Describe all transformations $F : \Sigma^\omega \to \Sigma^\omega$ (e.g.\ continuous, computable, or Turing functionals) such that $F(\omega)$ is Martin-Löf random whenever $\omega$ is Martin-Löf random.

Give an intrinsic characterization (algebraic, combinatorial, or computability-theoretic) of these randomness-preserving transformations on strings and on sequences.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Calude and Jürgensen and subsequent authors have shown that base-change and certain codings preserve Martin-Löf randomness (e.g., randomness is invariant under positional number representations), and recent work characterizes continuous transformations preserving 2-randomness. However, a complete intrinsic characterization of all randomness-preserving transformations on finite strings and on infinite sequences remains an active area of research rather than a settled theorem.

status_evidence.title: Randomness as an invariant for number representations
status_evidence.snippet: Calude and Jürgensen show usual positional representations of a real number are either random for all bases or for none.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on randomness preservation under base-change transformations.

status_evidence.title: Continuous randomness via transformations of 2-random sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2023) work studying continuous transformations and the randomness they preserve.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research on characterizing transformations preserving algorithmic randomness on sequences.
